coverage_gaps: Backward and forward citation-graph services are unavailable as direct routes; expansion must use PubMed-linked records and author or title searches, which may miss citations not indexed there.
Preprint servers are unavailable, so recent unpublished mechanistic results and their evolving status cannot be searched systematically.

Dedicated population-genetics resources such as ClinVar, GWAS Catalog, gnomAD and ancestry-specific variant databases are unavailable, limiting independent verification of variant classification and frequency.
Structural, proteomic and protein-knowledge databases are unavailable, limiting independent accession, structure and phosphosite cross-checks.
Patent databases are unavailable; therapeutic intellectual-property chronology remains outside scope.
FDA routing covers United States regulatory material only, leaving non-US regulator decisions and safety communications unassessed.
Full-text language translation and paywalled supplementary data availability may constrain assessment of otherwise eligible records.
exclusion_criteria: Records published, posted or effectively updated after 2024-12-31.
Parkinson disease papers that mention LRRK2 only incidentally and provide no genetic, mechanistic, substrate, physiological, biomarker, intervention or limiting evidence.
LRRK2 studies unrelated to Parkinson disease or parkinsonism unless they establish a physiological substrate, normal function or safety liability necessary to interpret the disease mechanism.
Purely computational predictions, docking studies or pathway enrichments lacking genetic, biochemical, cellular, organismal or clinical validation.
Studies that label a protein as an LRRK2 substrate solely from co-localization, interaction or correlated abundance without phosphorylation or perturbation evidence.
Conference abstracts, editorials, news items and commentaries lacking sufficient methods or primary data; they may serve only as leads to eligible records.
Non-primary review claims that cannot be traced to an eligible primary source.
Patents and commercial materials used as scientific evidence, because legal claims and marketing statements do not establish biological mechanism.
Duplicate reports of the same experiment with no additional data, while the most complete version and provenance links are retained.
Retracted records as affirmative support; they remain in the challenge ledger with their retraction status and affected claims.
inclusion_criteria: Records available on or before 2024-12-31 that directly address LRRK2 genetic discovery, Parkinson disease association, enzymatic mechanism, physiological substrates, downstream physiology, target engagement or mechanism-limiting evidence.
Primary human linkage, sequencing, association, penetrance, genotype-phenotype, pathology, biomarker or clinical trial evidence with identifiable population, variant and outcome definitions.
Biochemical, structural, cellular or animal studies that directly perturb or measure LRRK2 and provide controls sufficient to evaluate kinase, GTPase, localization or substrate claims.

Substrate studies that distinguish direct phosphorylation from interaction or pathway correlation through purified-protein assays, endogenous phosphosite measurement, genetic perturbation, pharmacological inhibition or orthogonal validation.
Null, negative, contradictory, failed-replication, nonpenetrance, loss-of-function, safety, correction and retraction evidence relevant to claim strength or generality.
Systematic reviews and authoritative narrative reviews only for terminology expansion, historical orientation and citation seeding; mechanistic conclusions must trace to eligible primary records.
All organisms and experimental systems are eligible when species, tissue, cell type and model limitations are recorded; human evidence is kept analytically separate from model evidence.
All publication languages are eligible when an English title or abstract supports screening, with translation needs recorded for otherwise eligible full texts.
Trial and regulatory records are linked to publications by NCT identifier, drug code, DOI, PMID or explicit sponsor-study identity while each source record and date remain independently preserved.

Duplicate occurrences are merged by PMID, DOI, trial identifier or regulatory record identity while preserving every query-to-record link; conflicting duplicate metadata are escalated for manual resolution.

question_frame: Target-mechanism evidence frame: for Parkinson disease, assess how human LRRK2 genetic discovery and disease-associated variants support causality; how LRRK2 kinase, ROC GTPase, COR and localization functions alter physiological substrate phosphorylation and downstream cell biology; and which penetrance, ancestry, model-system, biomarker, null, replication and intervention findings constrain mechanistic strength or generality. Search publications from 1990 through 2024-12-31, include human genetic and biomarker studies plus mammalian, cellular and biochemical mechanism studies, accept all languages when an English title or abstract permits eligibility assessment, and use reviews only for terminology and citation seeding.
stop_rules: Complete all planned PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov and FDA regulatory queries and record exact query, execution time, cutoff, result count and provider version for each run.
Do not begin broad screening until sentinel queries recover the named genetic-discovery, pathogenic-activation and Rab-substrate anchors or documented alias and indexing checks explain each miss.
Run discovery, confirmation, expansion, challenge and update waves independently before merging records by stable identifiers.

Continue backward, forward, author and linked-record expansion until two consecutive expansion passes add no decision-relevant eligible evidence to genetics, enzyme mechanism, substrates or limiting-evidence branches.

Require at least one challenge search for incomplete penetrance or ancestry heterogeneity, one for null or model-dependent mechanism findings, and one for corrections or retractions before declaring saturation.
Escalate unresolved variant nomenclature, conflicting duplicate metadata, uncertain publication dates and disagreement over direct-substrate status to manual review before synthesis.
Stop at the as_of boundary even when later records appear in provider results, retaining their identifiers only in a post-cutoff exclusion ledger.

Stop when planned sources are complete and additional retrieval cannot change the direction, confidence or stated scope of any major mechanistic conclusion; otherwise report the unsaturated branch as a coverage gap.
If time or record budget is reached before saturation, stop deterministically, preserve the last completed wave and identify every unrun query and affected evidence branch.
Keep mechanism and translational intervention branches separately traceable, and do not treat trial existence or target engagement alone as proof of clinical efficacy.
